transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-23 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Product), Samir Gupta (Aurora Head of AI), Leah Ortiz (Platform Eng), Tom Bennett (Security), Rita Kwan (Finance)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown; answered security questions; next step pilot and pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining - i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the account owner, um we have Diego and Priya with me who will do the deep bits.
[00:18] Samir: yep thanks Maya, we'll try to keep this high level, Leah is most interested in the per-route cost stuff, Tom has some compliance questions.
[00:30] Diego: great, i'll start with the Console -> usage analytics, so this is the per-route dashboard, you can see traffic, latency percentiles, cost per token by model and route. note: some names in the UI may read as Redwood counsel in the auto transcript ha.
[00:50] Leah: quick Q - how granular is the cost breakdown? can we get tenant-level?
[00:58] Diego: yes, you can slice by route, model version, and tenant tag; the console exposes per-token cost, egress, and infra delta. we also show batching efficiency and cache hit rates which factor into unit economics.
[01:20] Rita: finance: do we get historical trend export to csv? we want monthly run rates for forecasting.
[01:26] Maya: absolutely, export and scheduled reports are built in. we'll share a sample export after the call.
[01:40] Diego: walking through the dashboard now — here's a top-level view: requests per minute, p50/ p95/ p99 latencies, and a cost heatmap by route. in the demo tenant, you can see the query / embedding routes separated.
[02:10] Samir: can you show the routing policy stuff? we might want cheap-but-slower model for backfill and fast model for prod.
[02:18] Priya: sure - in our routing tab you can create policies by priority: latency SLO, cost target, region. if a primary model is unavailable it can fallback to a quantized variant or hosted fallback. i should say quantized variant may be slightly degraded on certain evals.
[02:45] Tom: security question — where do logs live? audit logs, do you integrate with our SIEM?
[02:53] Diego: audit logs export to your S3 or GCS bucket and we have connectors or you can stream to your SIEM via syslog. for private deployments the control plane can be customer-hosted. we support KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping.
[03:18] Tom: do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?
[03:22] Maya: yes BYOK via customer KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated, hosted has managed keys but we offer a KMS integration path for enterprise.
[03:34] Leah: what about SSO and RBAC? we need SCIM + SAML and SCIM provisioning so that groups map to team routes.
[03:40] Diego: yep SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC on routes/models. you can limit ability to change routing policies to admin roles.
[03:55] Samir: what's the diff between dedicated and private again? i'm fuzzy on the semantics.
[04:02] Priya: short: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools we run in our cloud with tenant isolation and commit blocks, good when you need predictable throughput and an SLA. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you a customer-managed control plane and network isolation, useful for regulated data or air-gapped setups.
[04:22] Samir: got it, and latency? we need 95th percentile under 200ms for our search use-case.
[04:30] Diego: that is achievable on Dedicated for most model families depending on sequence length; for hosted the p95 varies with batch and region. we'll include realistic numbers in the pilot.
[04:45] Leah: can you show an example of per-route cost breakdown?
[04:50] Diego: yes — here we have Route A (user search) vs Route B (assistant). the console shows tokens generated, tokens in, cost per-token, batching efficiency, cache hit rate, and estimated monthly spend. Route A is high request rate but short sequences, so cost-per-inference is low; Route B has longer sequences so higher per-request cost.
[05:20] Rita: finance: how do we estimate committed capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go?
[05:26] Maya: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet; committed capacity (Dedicated) gives unit discounts and reserved throughput, hosted is usage-based. We'll include examples with your estimated traffic to show breakeven points.
[05:48] Tom: about data residency — we operate in EU and need logs to stay in EU, can Redwood guarantee data residency?
[05:56] Priya: we have region routing and data residency controls. for Hosted you can pick region endpoints; Dedicated/Private give you stronger guarantees. we'll include language for contracts around residency and logging locations.
[06:18] Samir: any hiccups with model variants and eval drift when you switch quantized models?
[06:24] Diego: yes, quantization can affect quality. Console has an evals integration to monitor quality regressions tied to prompt sets — we can trigger alerts if quality drops beyond threshold after a rollout.
[06:44] Samir: cool. i want to see the actual export that ties back to tokens and cost.
[06:50] Diego: demoing export now — CSV has per-route daily rows, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, cost_token, total_cost. slight note: sometimes the exported columns have shorthand model names in the transcript, like redwood-rlm being read weird.
[07:14] Leah: operationally, on our side, the infra team will run a pilot with a replay of last month's traffic. how invasive is the instrumentation?
[07:22] Diego: minimal — you can route a copy of traffic to Redwood endpoints or run a dry-run via our SDK. for Dedicated/Private we can also provide a small on-prem agent for controlled testing.
[07:36] Samir: about throughput — we saw a doc that mentioned KV cache and continuous batching — can you explain quickly?
[07:44] Priya: KV cache is for chat-like workloads — it keeps key-value cache across tokens to avoid re-computing prefixes. continuous batching groups requests to improve GPU utilization while respecting latency SLOs. the console shows batching efficiency metric so you can tune target latencies vs cost.
[08:05] Rita: finance: any surprise costs? network egress, for example?
[08:10] Diego: egress is itemized in the cost export; if you do high-embedding workloads, the cost can be dominated by compute; we'll highlight that.
[08:24] Samir: competitor note — we've evaluated OpenAI endpoints, but their multi-tenant costs were higher for our volumes. we also have an internal self-hosted effort but ops overhead is large.
[08:36] Maya: makes sense — our console aims to make the economics visible.
[08:48] Diego: jumping back to routing, you can create per-route quotas, throttles, and weighted routing between model families for A/B tests and canarying.
[09:02] Leah: is there a way to alert if cost for a route spikes unexpectedly?
[09:07] Diego: yes, alerts can be set on cost rate, tokens per minute, latency percentiles, and you can auto-failover to cheaper model or throttle when budget exceeded.
[09:24] Samir: for the pilot we want per-route benchmarks comparing hosted vs dedicated with our traffic shape. what's the timeframe?
[09:30] Maya: we can stand up a 1-week pilot within two weeks; Diego will provide scripts; we need your sample traffic and a signed pilot agreement (low friction).
[09:44] Tom: security follow-up: can you provide the SOC2 cert and encryption in transit docs?
[09:49] Maya: yes, we'll share the security pack and KMS integration guide in the next email.
[10:02] Diego: quick demo — here's the per-route detail page, shows cost line items: model compute, infra allocation, batching savings, caching savings, and third-party egress. you can toggle time windows and compare versions.
[10:27] Leah: can we tie routes to internal cost centers for chargeback?
[10:31] Diego: yep route tags map to cost centers; exports include tag columns so finance can ingest.
[10:40] Rita: good. what about SLA baked into Dedicated? we need 99.9% and p95 latency commitments.
[10:48] Priya: Dedicated has SLA tiers; we'll put specifics in the contract appendix. for extreme latency SLOs we sometimes recommend pinning model families and pre-warming KV caches.
[11:05] Samir: any limitations on model families? like can we bring huggingface weights?
[11:10] Diego: we onboard open model weights we certify; for Private we can support customer-provided models subject to licensing and runtime compatibility.
[11:24] Maya: quick note: sometimes the transcript engine flattens names - redwoo rather than Redwood, apologies.
[11:34] Tom: what's the rollback strategy if a new model degrades quality?
[11:38] Priya: rollout policies support automatic rollback on regression triggers; you can set thresholds on eval metrics or QA prompts.
[11:50] Samir: ok, let's talk numbers — can you show an example cost table for our projected 50M tokens/month?
[11:58] Diego: showing a sample table: hosted pay-as-you-go estimate: $X/month (we'll replace X with real number in pricing sheet), Dedicated committed gives ~20-35% unit discount depending on commit. caching and batching can further reduce effective unit cost.
[12:20] Rita: finance will need a simple pdf with assumptions.
[12:24] Maya: yes will provide.
[12:30] Diego: I'll also show the route-level drilldown where you can click a route and see historical cost, which models served it, and the percent of requests served by cache.
[12:46] Leah: for the pilot, we want to test 3 routes: search, assist, and rerank. can you ensure the pilot includes per-route SLA metrics?
[12:54] Maya: yes pilot scope will include those three routes and per-route metrics and a short report at the end.
[13:05] Tom: what about logging PII - do you redact automatically?
[13:11] Diego: we provide redaction hooks and you can opt to scrub logs before storage; for private deployments you control retention.
[13:26] Samir: any legal red flags? we have some HIPAA-adjacent customers but not strictly healthcare.
[13:33] Tom: we will share the list of compliance requirements, but SOC2 and ISO are the primary ones.
[13:40] Maya: understood.
[13:52] Priya: one more console feature — cost projection engine: uses historical traffic and model mix to project monthly spend under different configurations. it's helpful to see the impact of switching to a quantized variant or increasing batch windows.
[14:12] Rita: can you run a scenario where we push more to cached responses? what's the savings?
[14:18] Diego: in demo data, going from 10% cache hit to 40% hit reduced compute spend by ~18% depending on route. real numbers will vary.
[14:34] Samir: any gotchas with burst capacity? we sometimes have flash sales.
[14:39] Priya: we offer burst capacity on Dedicated; for Hosted we have autoscale but can hit regional capacity constraints. console will show capacity headroom and recommended burst plan.
[14:58] Leah: can we do per-route throttles for burst protection?
[15:03] Diego: yes you can set per-route QPS and burst buffers.
[15:18] Maya: ok nearing the end — recap and next steps?
[15:22] Samir: recap: pilot for 3 routes, run benchmarks hosted vs dedicated, get pricing, security docs.
[15:29] Maya: awesome. action items: i will send pricing and pilot agreement; Diego will post the pilot runbook and scripts; Tom will send the compliance checklist.
[15:39] Rita: finance will review the pricing and come back with preferred commit level.
[15:45] Maya: great, we'll aim to schedule the pilot kickoff for 2026-07-06 pending paperwork.
[15:52] Samir: sounds good thanks everyone.
[15:55] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with an email incl security pack and pricing. bye.
